detail: The ICJ judgment in The Gambia v. Myanmar is scheduled for 10:00 The Hague time (09:00 UTC, 16:00 WIB) today, read by President Yuji Iwasawa in a public sitting expected to last up to 90 minutes; the ruling is final and binding, with no appeal. Reuters reported about 1.2 million Rohingya in the Cox's Bazar camps in Bangladesh will follow the judgment, with some 550,000 still in Myanmar. PENDING: the verdict had not been delivered at collection time (~06:45 UTC); the builder must insert the actual finding when it lands.
fact: judgment due 10:00 The Hague time; final, no appeal
headline: World Court to deliver Rohingya genocide judgment at 10:00 in The Hague
summary: The ICJ delivers its judgment today in The Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar; a genocide finding would be the first ever against a state, and the ruling is final.

detail: Adoption of the Shenzhen Declaration is targeted for today, Nov 19, before the 33rd APEC leaders' meeting closes; Deputy Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu said it would set out a roadmap toward an Asia-Pacific community on four pillars - trade, connectivity, innovation and development - with a standalone FTAAP statement and an AI cooperation document also prepared. The day is set to end with the first Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral, with a separate Trump-Putin meeting; the Kremlin has discussed a possible joint communique, while a senior US official said no agreement is expected. PENDING: neither the declaration text nor any trilateral output had been issued at collection time (~06:45 UTC).
fact: declaration adoption targeted for today, Nov 19
headline: APEC leaders set to adopt Shenzhen Declaration as summit closes
summary: APEC's Shenzhen Declaration is targeted for adoption today before the summit closes, and the first Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral caps the day; no agreement is expected.

detail: Released on Wednesday by the APEC CEO Summit 2026, the Shenzhen Initiative calls for deepening an open regional economy, driving inclusive growth through technological innovation, strengthening regional connectivity and working together for shared prosperity, under four priorities: openness and inclusiveness, innovation-driven growth, greater connectivity and mutually beneficial cooperation. Xinhua reported it is the first time in the summit's 30-year history that an outcome document has been issued in the form of an initiative, and that it commits the business community to fully implement the Putrajaya Vision 2040.
fact: first CEO Summit outcome document in 30 years
headline: APEC CEO Summit issues first-ever Shenzhen Initiative
summary: The APEC CEO Summit released the Shenzhen Initiative, its first outcome document in 30 years, backing an open regional economy and the Putrajaya Vision 2040.

detail: Evacuation is now under way, not just planned: 46,701 people had already been moved to safer locations by Thursday, with 448 cyclone shelters operational and another 3,000 being prepared, 60 ODRAF and 14 NDRF teams deployed, and a red alert covering 11 districts. The IMD's 05:30 IST bulletin put severe cyclonic storm Akvan at 14.5N, 85.3E, about 530 km south of Gopalpur and 590 km south of Puri, moving north-northwest to cross the coast between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon on Nov 20 with maximum sustained winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110.
headline: Odisha moves 46,701 people to shelters as Cyclone Akvan closes in
summary: Odisha has evacuated 46,701 people as severe Cyclone Akvan bears down on the coast, with landfall due near Gopalpur around noon on Nov 20.

detail: Anthropic's Class A shares (ticker ANT) are due to begin trading today, Thu Nov 19, on the Nasdaq Global Select Market after pricing at $83 a share on Nov 18 - above the $70-78 range - in an offering of 980 million shares. The regular session opens at 09:30 ET (14:30 UTC, 21:30 WIB), and a listing of this size typically prints its first trade later in the session once the opening auction clears; no opening price had been reported by any outlet at collection time (~06:45 UTC). PENDING: first trade and early price action versus the $83 IPO price still to come.
fact: Nasdaq opens 14:30 UTC; first trade still pending
headline: Anthropic shares set to open on Nasdaq after record $81.3bn IPO
summary: Anthropic's ANT stock starts trading on Nasdaq today after the record $81.3bn IPO at $83 a share; the first print is expected later in the US session.

detail: Palestinian medics said an Israeli airstrike near the army raid in central Gaza killed one person, and separate strikes killed two other people in Deir al-Balah and Gaza City on Wednesday, as Israeli tanks rolled onto the main Salahudeen road west of the Yellow Line. The Board of Peace's 12-page second report to the UN Security Council accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments and warned that 'a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely'; senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as 'pure disinformation'. Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire took effect, while Israel says five of its soldiers have been killed.
fact: peace board warns ceasefire cannot be sustained
headline: Three killed in Gaza strikes as peace board warns ceasefire may collapse
summary: Three Palestinians were killed in Gaza strikes as the Board of Peace warned both sides are failing the ceasefire, which it said cannot be sustained.

detail: The third attack in a week, overnight into Thursday, struck the bridge's railway section - the part left standing after strikes on Nov 16-17 destroyed a 227-metre section of the road span, a collapse BBC Verify has now verified. Crimea's Russian-installed governor Sergei Aksyonov said traffic had been temporarily halted after the new attack and damage was being assessed; The Guardian reported around 2,000 vehicles waiting on either side of the crossing while inspections took place. Ukraine has not claimed responsibility for Wednesday's attack in The Guardian's reporting.
fact: third strike in a week hit the railway section
headline: Third attack on Crimean Bridge hits railway section, halting all traffic
summary: A third attack in a week hit the Crimean Bridge's railway section overnight, halting road and rail traffic after a 227-metre road span was destroyed.

detail: The 18-page presidency draft of the cover decision, released on Monday by negotiations president Chris Bowen of Australia, calls for an 'immediate transition away from fossil fuels' in energy systems, a tripling of adaptation finance to at least $120 billion a year by 2035, and raising electrification to 35% of final energy use by 2035; EU climate commissioner Wopke Hoekstra has publicly criticised the draft. The text's 144 provisions must be agreed by consensus, with ministers now handling the hardest questions before the summit closes on Friday, Nov 20.
fact: draft needs consensus by Friday, Nov 20 close
headline: COP31 ministers take over as fossil-fuel wording splits the final draft
summary: COP31's draft demands an immediate fossil-fuel transition and $120bn in adaptation finance, but ministers must forge consensus by Friday's close.

detail: Iran's foreign ministry said late on Wednesday that its forces had struck US Patriot air-defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms in self-defence, after US fighter jets hit a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday night. Kuwait's military said its air defences responded to hostile drones targeting the Ali Al Salem air base and reported no casualties or damage; Bahrain said it intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks, its fourth in six days. Qatar warned the strikes threatened talks to end the war, and Iran's army chief Amir Hatami warned of a 'more devastating' reaction to any new US attack. The kinetic exchange itself took place on Wednesday, Nov 18; Thursday's developments are the diplomatic fallout.
fact: Tehran calls strikes self-defence; Qatar warns talks
headline: Iran calls Gulf strikes self-defence as Qatar warns peace talks at risk
summary: Iran justified its strikes on US assets in Kuwait and Bahrain as self-defence, while Qatar warned the escalation threatens talks to end the war.
